entrypoints.summary: RegistrationRequest and RegistrationResponse carry serialized OPRF group elements across a trust boundary; the finding also identifies affected received-message deserializers.

affected_components.role: The audit's printed vulnerable deserialization and its described downstream evaluation path.

code_slices.fixed: The report describes a fix that verifies deserialized group elements are not identity elements and rejects identity elements in the named received messages.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The received registration request reaches CreateRegistrationResponse, which invokes OPRF Evaluate using the supplied group element.
code_slices.vulnerable: RegistrationRequest::deserialize decodes alpha using CS::Group::from_element_slice after a size check and returns it without a neutral-point check.

observability.channel: test suite and protocol-derived keying value
negative_controls: Fixed deserializers reject identity elements in the named message types.
The report does not provide an end-to-end observed export_key value.
observability.positive_marker: The report states that neutral-point propagation may force export_key to a known value; its test mutation caused random_ristretto_point to return neutral points while all existing tests continued to pass.

preconditions: Ability to submit an OPAQUE registration or related received message across the protocol trust boundary.
A vulnerable deserializer that accepts a serialized identity OPRF element.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A serialized OPRF identity/neutral group element.
trigger_steps.summary: Encode the neutral point in a serialized OPRF group-element field of a received OPAQUE message so the element is accepted by deserialization.

relation_candidates.rationale: A received protocol message can carry a serialized OPRF element, including the neutral point when deserialization does not reject it.

relation_candidates.dst: Propagate a neutral point through OPRF evaluation
relation_candidates.rationale: The accepted identity element is multiplied by the server private scalar in Evaluate and remains neutral.

relation_candidates.rationale: The report states that neutral-point propagation may ultimately reach export_key and force it to a known value.
relation_candidates.src: Propagate a neutral point through OPRF evaluation

relation_candidates.dst: Reject identity OPRF elements at deserialization
relation_candidates.rationale: The reported fix rejects identity elements in received message deserializers.

impact.affected_asset: OPAQUE export_key and secrecy properties dependent on valid OPRF processing.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a security-degenerate neutral group element to propagate through OPRF processing by submitting it in a received serialized protocol message.
impact.security_effect: Potential loss of secrecy for a keying value: export_key may be forced to a known value.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker able to supply an OPAQUE message at the protocol trust boundary supplies a serialized OPRF group element encoding the neutral (identity) point.
RegistrationRequest::deserialize size-checks and decodes with CS::Group::from_element_slice but does not reject the neutral point, allowing the decoded alpha identity element to be returned.

CreateRegistrationResponse passes the received element to OPRF Evaluate, where multiplication by the server private scalar leaves the identity input as the neutral point; the report describes analogous flows in other messages.
The resulting degenerate point operations can zero out subsequent processing and may force export_key to a known value.

failure.operation: Scalar multiplication of an attacker-provided identity OPRF element in OPRF Evaluate, yielding the neutral point.

primary_invariant.statement: Every deserialized OPRF group element in a received OPAQUE message must be non-neutral.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The affected deserializers accepted a mathematically decodable identity element because from_element_slice did not itself enforce non-neutrality and no subsequent neutral-point test was made at the deserialization boundary.

raw_refs.role: authoritative finding report and reviewed code excerpt

quality.review_notes: The public audit directly documents the finding, historical deserializer excerpt, causal OPRF evaluation path, test mutation, recommendation, and retest status. The export_key consequence remains qualified as 'may' by the report; no immutable raw historical source, patch diff, or end-to-end identity-message harness is present in this bundle. The changelog artifact was not used for mechanism or remediation claims because its inspected excerpt did not establish this historical fix.

remediation.invariant_restored: All received serialized OPRF group elements are rejected when they encode the identity element, preventing neutral-point propagation into OPRF operations.
mitigation_classes: Reject neutral/identity group elements during inbound message deserialization
Ensure generated client and server scalars are non-zero
Add serialization regression tests for identity-element rejection

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker must be able to provide a received OPAQUE message whose serialized group-element field encodes the identity point.
data_structure_invariants: Inbound serialized OPRF elements must decode to non-neutral group elements.
Library-generated OPRF scalars must be non-zero.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The report associates zero scalar and neutral group-element behavior with predictable neutral results; this finding's immediate input is a serialized neutral group element.
numeric_domains.name: OPRF scalar

state_context.state_machine: Received OPAQUE registration/credential message -> deserialize group element -> OPRF Evaluate -> later OPRF processing and possible export_key derivation.

target.component: OPRF group-element message deserialization in src/messages.rs

oracle.expected_negative: A pre-fix deserializer accepts an identity element; the report's mutation of random_ristretto_point to produce neutral points states that all existing tests continued to pass.
oracle.expected_positive: A regression test should reject serialized identity elements for RegistrationRequest, RegistrationResponse, CredentialRequest, and CredentialResponse.
